source.title: Mechanistic Convergence and Divergence Across LLM Instances: Axes of Correspondence for Generalizable Interpretability Research

page_placements.theme: Previous-token heads: generic role, consistent timing, data dependence

record.file_problem: The text is complete. Its internal title and venue (Toward a Theory of Generalizability in LLM Mechanistic Interpretability Research; NeurIPS 2025) differ from the supplied title and venue.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses induction heads and in-context learning as context for its framework, but its own empirical study measures 1-back attention, not induction heads or induction-driven in-context learning.
record.gate_note: The induction-head and in-context-learning findings cited from other work are not this study's results. The empirical case study measures attention to the immediately preceding token; it does not establish induction behavior, a previous-token/induction-head circuit, or a link to in-context learning. Its 1-back attention results are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The paper discusses induction heads only as a conceptual example, citing other work. Its own experiment measures 1-back (previous-token) attention in Pythia seeds. It does not identify induction heads, measure [A][B]…[A]→[B] behaviour, test composition with induction heads, or measure in-context learning. Its results bear on no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The case study supports the proposed correspondence axes: 1-back attention is consistent in when but not where it appears, and larger models show earlier onset, steeper slope and higher peak. The authors also note that the heads' functional role was not tested.
record.recipe_differences: The empirical method measures attention to the immediately preceding token across Pythia seeds and checkpoints. It does not reproduce an induction-head or in-context-learning measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: Model size was associated with changes in 1-back attention onset, slope, and peak. Positional patterns varied across seeds and architectures. The paper reports similar developmental results under alternative 1-back attention operationalizations and across Natural Stories Corpus stories.

fits_no_version.finding: 1-back attention rises around 10^3 steps (about 2B tokens) across Pythia 14M–410M seeds. Larger models show earlier onset, steeper slope and higher peak. Trajectories correlate highly within and across sizes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Previous-token (1-back) attention develops at a consistent point in pretraining across seeds and sizes, with timing and magnitude scaling with model size.

fits_no_version.finding: The layer position of 1-back heads varies across seeds and sizes. 14M seeds split between layer 3 and layer 4, and later layers show less 1-back attention (β=−0.11).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The location of previous-token heads is much less consistent across model instances than their developmental timing.

fits_no_version.finding: In a regression on pairwise trajectory correlations, Same Model β=0.05 and log parameters β=0.03, so larger different-size models converge more. MDS separation ratios are 14M 11.4, 70M 3.37, 160M 2.42, 410M 4.0. No row records these.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Developmental convergence of previous-token attention across architectures increases with model size.

record.problems: The authors explicitly note that candidate 1-back heads were defined by attention behavior and their functional role in predictions was not investigated. The empirical sample is limited to four Pythia sizes, their random seeds, and a shared training setup; it does not directly test induction heads or in-context learning.
record.rows_left_out: Cited results about induction heads and ICL were excluded because they are from other work. Individual seed/head trajectories shown in Figures 1, 2, and 4 were not extracted separately; the text reports aggregate trends and specific statistical results instead.

untested.parts: Previous-token heads are measured only by attention pattern. Composition with induction heads and the induction mechanism are not tested.
No induction-head emergence, in-context-learning gain or loss bump is measured. The onset around 10^3 steps is for 1-back attention only.
Induction behaviour is not measured. Universality is shown only for 1-back attention, across Pythia seeds and sizes.
Training data and setup are not varied.

record.verdict_notes: The text is the arXiv/NeurIPS 2025 version, not the CL journal version the DOI names. Induction-head statements (universality, shared trajectories, relative position, ICL debate) are cited from Olsson et al. and Singh et al. and are not this study's results. The 1-back heads resemble the previous-token heads of V1, but no composition or induction test is done, so no row is linked to V1.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test induction-head formation, composition with a previous-token head, or the [A][B] … [A] → [B] mechanism.
Does not measure induction-head emergence, in-context-learning gains, or a training-loss bump.
Does not test induction heads as a cause of most in-context learning in large transformers.
Measures 1-back attention in Pythia models only; it does not test induction behavior across model families, architectures, or modalities.
Does not vary training data or setup to test their effects on induction heads or in-context learning.
Does not test few-shot task learning or compare induction heads with other mechanisms for that behavior.
Does not test whether induction-head formation comprises multiple transitions.

rows.subject: Pythia-14M, Pythia-70M, Pythia-160M, and Pythia-410M (all tested seeds)
rows.operation_detail: Measured maximum 1-back attention across seeds and checkpoints; fit a GAM using log training step.

conditions.value: 16 per model; available checkpoints up to and including step 1000, followed by steps 1000, 50000, 100000, and 143000

rows.measure: Maximum 1-back attention over training; GAM fit to all data points
rows.value: GAM R² = 0.95; predictions were consistent with an expected onset between 512 and 2000 steps. The text also describes onset around 10³ training steps, corresponding to roughly 2B tokens of exposure.
rows.note: Aggregate result across models and seeds, as reported by the study. This is a developmental result for 1-back attention, not induction heads.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for the induction-head claim versions. The 1-back attention GAM has R²=0.95 and an expected onset between 512 and 2000 steps.
source_check.problem: The measured 1-back attention effect does not establish any induction-head claim version; versions=none is appropriate.

rows.subject: Pythia suite (all tested seeds)
rows.operation_detail: Regressed each seed's 1-back attention onset measure on log parameter count, with seed as a random intercept.

conditions.value: earliest step where change in maximum 1-back attention relative to change in log training step exceeded a threshold; averaged over thresholds 0.01 to 0.3

rows.measure: Association of log parameters with 1-back attention onset
rows.value: β = −0.18, SE = 0.05, p < .001; larger models had reduced onset (earlier onset).
rows.note: Reported as a separate mixed-effects model result.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for the induction-head claim versions. The association with 1-back attention onset is β=−0.18, SE=0.05, p<.001.
source_check.problem: Earlier onset of 1-back attention does not establish an induction-head effect.

rows.subject: Pythia suite (all tested seeds)
rows.operation_detail: Regressed each seed's maximum 1-back attention on log parameter count, with seed as a random intercept.
rows.measure: Association of log parameters with slope of maximum 1-back attention over log training step
rows.value: β = 0.01, SE = 0.003, p < .001; larger models had increased slope.
rows.note: Slope was obtained by regressing maximum 1-back attention at each step against log training step.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for the induction-head claim versions. The slope association is β=0.01, SE=0.003, p<.001; the dependent variable regressed against log parameters was each seed's estimated trajectory slope.
source_check.problem: The measured slope concerns 1-back attention, not induction; the operation description also omits that slope was the dependent variable.

rows.subject: Pythia suite (all tested seeds)
rows.operation_detail: Regressed each seed's peak 1-back attention on log parameter count, with seed as a random intercept.
rows.measure: Association of log parameters with peak maximum 1-back attention
rows.value: β = 0.07, SE = 0.01, p < 0.001; larger models had a higher peak.
rows.note: Peak was defined as the maximum 1-back attention across steps for each seed.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for the induction-head claim versions. The peak 1-back attention association is β=0.07, SE=0.01, p<0.001.
source_check.problem: Peak 1-back attention does not measure an induction-head claim version.

rows.subject: Pythia suite (all tested model instances)
rows.operation_detail: Measured average 1-back attention by head and modeled it against layer depth.
rows.measure: Effect of layer depth on average 1-back attention
rows.value: β = −0.11, SE = 0.005, p < 0.001; later layers were associated with less attention to previous tokens on average.
rows.note: Authors describe positional consistency across architectures as relatively low, with some evidence for a peak in middle layers.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for the induction-head claim versions. Layer depth predicts average 1-back attention at the final step with β=−0.11, SE=0.005, p<0.001.
source_check.locator_found: Section 4.2.1; Figure 2 and the paragraph continuing after it.
source_check.problem: The positional result concerns putative 1-back heads and cannot establish an induction-head effect.

rows.subject: Pythia seeds of the same architecture
rows.operation_detail: Calculated Pearson correlations between pairs of 1-back attention trajectories.

conditions.value: seeds belonging to the same architecture

rows.note: The paper reports this as an average over same-architecture seed pairs.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for the induction-head claim versions. Same-architecture trajectory correlations are M=0.99, SD=0.04.
source_check.problem: Correlated 1-back attention trajectories do not establish correlated induction-head development.

rows.subject: Pythia seeds of different architectures
rows.operation_detail: Calculated Pearson correlations between pairs of 1-back attention trajectories.
rows.note: The paper reports this as an average over different-architecture instance pairs; it also reports that larger different architectures had higher correlations.
rows.check: The state 'partial' has no version to be judged against. This is a comparator row (different-architecture correlation, M = 0.95 vs 0.99 within architecture), not a partial effect.

rows.subject: Pythia-14M
rows.operation_detail: Compared maximum 1-back attention trajectories across random seeds and Natural Stories Corpus stories.

conditions.value: each story from the Natural Stories Corpus

rows.value: The trajectories were described as extremely similar, with changes in attention beginning around 10³ training steps for all seeds and stories.
rows.note: Aggregate qualitative result across the reported seeds and stories.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for the induction-head claim versions. Across Pythia-14M seeds and stories, 1-back attention trajectories are described as extremely similar, with changes beginning around 10^3 training steps.
source_check.problem: Consistency of 1-back attention across stories does not establish an induction-head claim version.

relation.reason: Sections 3.1–3.2 discuss induction circuits, their proposed generalizability, and debate about their role in in-context learning using cited research.

tranche.reason: The empirical study measures immediately preceding-token attention, a related but different construct. It neither tests induction behavior or in-context learning nor uses induction heads as an experimental tool.

source_check.notes: The authors-conclusion paraphrase is accurate; Section 4.3 explicitly says the heads' functional role in predictions was not investigated. Source metadata differ from the pack: the supplied text is titled Toward a Theory of Generalizability in LLM Mechanistic Interpretability Research, dated September 2025, with a NeurIPS 2025 designation.
